The senators said delays could prevent students and exchange visitors from reaching the US in time for the beginning of the academic year.

Article Title: Two killed as US Army Apache helicopter crashes near Fort Hood base in Texas
Article Text:
The Apache was out on a routine training flight

An Apache helicopter of the US Army crashed in a central Texas field on Wednesday (local time), killing both people aboard and sparking a wildfire that forced the evacuation of several homes.A video from the site showed rescue workers and firefighters walking through a charred field as plumes of dark smoke rose from flames still burning around the wreckage.Officials at nearby Fort Hood confirmed that an AH-64 Apache had crashed. Cliff Coleman, spokesman for the Bell County Sheriff’s Office, confirmed the deaths of both occupants and described the incident as a “violent crash.”The cause of the crash was not immediately known. Fort Hood’s criminal investigation division was leading the inquiry, Coleman added.The helicopter did not strike any homes or other structures when it crashed, he noted.According to another military official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, the Apache was on a routine training flight when the incident occurred.Fort Hood is a massive military installation spanning 214,968 acres (336 square miles) and is used to train and deploy heavy forces. The US Army describes the rolling, arid terrain around the base as an “ideal training ground.”The base has seen other fatal training accidents. In November 2015, four soldiers died when a Black Hawk helicopter crashed during an exercise. In 2016, nine Fort Hood soldiers were killed after a rain-swollen creek swept their vehicle into rushing waters.The AH-64 Apache has been a key part of the US military’s fleet since the first versions entered service in 1984. Its two-person crew sits in tandem, with the pilot in the rear and the co-pilot/gunner in the front.
Article Summary: Apache helicopter of the US Army crashes in central Texas, killing both people aboard. Crash sparks a wildfire that forced the evacuation of several homes. Fort Hood’s criminal investigation division is leading the inquiry. The cause of the crash was not immediately known.

Article Title: Georgia high school shooting leaves student injured, teenage suspect arrested
Article Text:
The suspect was arrested “without further incident” in a neighbourhood around 800 metres from the school

A shooting at a high school in Georgia has left one student injured, while a teenage suspect was taken into custody after fleeing the scene, police said.The incident at Warner Robins High School, involving two ninth-grade students, took place just one week into the new school year. Dozens of law enforcement officers responded to the school in Warner Robins, about 164 km south-east of Atlanta.Sheriff Matt Moulton said a group of students were inside a school bathroom when a verbal argument between two students escalated into a physical fight. One student was shot at about 2.15pm before the suspect fled.A school resource officer arrived quickly, applied tourniquets to the injured student and stayed until emergency medical personnel arrived. The student was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.About an hour later, the suspect was arrested “without further incident” in a neighbourhood around 800 metres from the school, Moulton said.“The school threat protocol and our training was followed perfectly today,” he said, adding that the incident could have had a much worse outcome.Houston County Schools Superintendent Richard Rogers said the school would be closed to students on Thursday and Friday. Crisis counsellors will be available for staff on Friday and students on Monday.
Article Summary: Incident at Warner Robins High School involved two ninth-grade students. One student was shot at about 2.15pm before the suspect fled. The student was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. About an hour later, the suspect was arrested ‘without further incident’

Article Title: In 2025, Virginia spent $8 million rebuilding 1.09 miles of Ragged Island shoreline; the project created 2.6 acres of new marsh and 2.2 acres of oyster reef while cutting hundreds of tons of sediment
Article Text:
Virginia’s Ragged Island restoration is creating new marsh and oyster habitat while reducing sediment entering Chesapeake Bay.

Ragged Island shoreline has faced decades of erosion

Breakwaters are helping rebuild the shoreline

Baby oysters are already growing

Restored marsh could benefit birds and wildlife

Project could reduce pollution in Chesapeake Bay

Restoration also stores carbon and reduces flooding

‘It’s really fun to see’

Virginia has completed a major shoreline restoration project on Ragged Island, helping rebuild wetlands and oyster habitat while reducing the amount of sediment and nutrients entering the Chesapeake Bay.The project, funded with $8 million from NOAA Fisheries’ Office of Habitat Conservation, was carried out by the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources and Ducks Unlimited. According to NOAA Fisheries, project partners installed breakwater structures along 1.09 miles of shoreline to protect the marsh from erosion and restore habitat.Ragged Island is a 1,500-acre brackish marsh where the James River meets the Chesapeake Bay. For decades, wind, waves and rising sea levels have gradually eaten away at the shoreline.Since 1937, hundreds of feet of marsh have disappeared. In some areas, erosion has left exposed walls of black soil several feet high, while saltwater has killed trees and other vegetation farther inland.The loss of marsh has also contributed to sediment and nutrient pollution entering the Chesapeake Bay. This can fuel algal blooms, reduce water quality and create conditions that are harmful to fish and other marine life.“In the past, when I drove along the shoreline in my boat, the water looked like chocolate milk,” said Chad Boyce, a fisheries biologist with the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources.“Suspended sediment can cause their gills to be irritated and fish often leave these areas to seek better water quality. Turbid water also makes it difficult for predator fish like red drum to find prey,” he added.In 2025, construction crews installed 62 low rock breakwaters offshore from the marsh. The structures reduce the energy of waves before they reach the shoreline while still allowing tides, fish and other aquatic species to move through gaps between the rocks.Excavators placed sand behind the breakwaters, creating shallow mounds known as “tombolos”. These areas trap sediment and gradually build new marsh habitat.The project has created approximately 2.6 acres of new marshland and 2.2 acres of oyster reef. The restored areas provide habitat for fish, crabs and other wildlife while helping protect existing marsh.The breakwaters are also keeping about 260 tons of sediment and nutrients from entering the Chesapeake Bay each year.Overall, the project is expected to prevent more than 500,000 pounds of suspended sediment, 70 pounds of nitrogen and 400 pounds of phosphorus from entering the bay annually.A visit to the project site in May 2026 showed early signs that the restoration is working. At low tide, baby oysters could be seen growing on the reef shelves, while sand was accumulating behind the breakwaters.Cordgrass planted along the shoreline is also taking root. As the plants grow, their roots will help hold sediment in place and strengthen the new marsh.The developing oyster reefs are expected to provide important habitat for a variety of fish.“Along with the fisheries habitat in the marsh, the new oyster reefs are a mecca for fish,” said David Norris, regional wildlife manager for the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources.“Baby fish love the structure of oyster reefs where they can get in and hide. A lot of the commercially viable fish populations will use it — red drum, croaker, flounder — along with other species,” Norris added.Striped bass, river herring, blue crabs and even endangered Atlantic sturgeon can also use the habitat as it continues to develop.The restoration is expected to provide benefits beyond fish and oysters. As submerged aquatic vegetation returns, it could create additional feeding habitat for waterfowl.“Submerged aquatic vegetation is probably the most important food resource in the Chesapeake Bay for waterfowl,” said Ed Farley, manager of conservation programs for Ducks Unlimited.“As the marsh goes away, really important habitat for wildlife also disappears,” he added.The restored area could eventually attract waterfowl species including canvasbacks, greater scaup and blue- and green-winged teal.Shoreline erosion in watersheds that feed the Chesapeake Bay accounts for approximately 57% of all sediment entering the bay, according to the Chesapeake Bay Program.The sediment can contribute to algal blooms that reduce oxygen levels in the water and place additional stress on marine life.“The Chesapeake Bay has had issues for the last 50 years with algal blooms caused by sedimentation,” Norris said. “Algal blooms can lead to low oxygen conditions, and cause major stress or even kill the organisms living there.”By slowing erosion and trapping sediment, the Ragged Island project is helping address part of that larger problem.The restored marsh is expected to provide climate and flood protection benefits as well. Wetlands store carbon in their soils, preventing it from being released when the land erodes.“We are also storing hundreds of thousands of tons of carbon right in this area that would have been released to the atmosphere as soon as it eroded away,” Norris said.“Not only are we protecting existing carbon, but every year there's more carbon being added to the marsh,” he added.The marsh also helps reduce flooding around nearby properties. During heavy tides and storms, wetlands can absorb and hold water, reducing the amount that reaches surrounding neighborhoods.The restoration has also helped improve opportunities for fishing and hunting in the area.“I've heard that the fishing's been excellent since the project's been completed,” Farley said. “It's really fun to see.”Norris said the project’s location makes its progress particularly visible to the public.“I'm incredibly proud of this project, not only because of the habitat we are protecting but also because of the location,” he said.“We’re at the foot of the James River Bridge across from Newport News, Virginia. Thousands of people drive across the bridge every day and can see the work we're doing. Not only do people get to see it, but they also get to use it,” Norris added.NOAA Fisheries is funding dozens of habitat restoration projects across the Chesapeake Bay. Together, these efforts aim to rebuild habitat for fish, oysters, blue crabs and other marine species while supporting the communities, fishing activities and tourism industries that depend on a healthy bay.
Article Summary: Virginia has completed a major shoreline restoration project on Ragged Island. The project has created 2.6 acres of new marshland and 2.2 acres of oyster reef. The restored areas provide habitat for fish, crabs and other wildlife. The breakwaters are also keeping about 260 tons of sediment and nutrients from entering the Chesapeake Bay.

Article Title: Louisiana created 1,170 acres of new wetlands in Barataria Basin; one year later, shrimp and crabs are returning to the restored habitat
Article Text:
One year after Louisiana restored 1,170 acres of wetlands, shrimp, crabs and red drum are returning to the habitat.

Louisiana’s wetlands have faced decades of land loss

1,170 acres of wetlands created

Shrimp, crabs and red drum are using the new habitat

‘It’s a big win’

Restored wetlands could benefit Louisiana’s economy

Restoration work will continue for decades

Louisiana’s coastline is showing early signs of recovery after a major wetland restoration project created 1,170 acres of new marsh habitat in the Barataria Basin. Just one year after construction, species including white and brown shrimp, blue crab and red drum have begun using the newly restored ecosystem.According to NOAA Fisheries, the Upper Barataria Marsh Creation Project is part of a larger effort by NOAA and its partners to rebuild Louisiana’s coastal habitats following decades of land loss and the damage caused by the 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill.Located between the Mississippi River and Bayou Lafourche, the Barataria Basin’s wetlands provide important benefits to Louisiana’s coastal communities. They support wildlife, fisheries and ecosystems that are closely connected to the region’s economy.However, the basin has lost nearly 300,000 acres of land since the 1930s. Erosion, storm surge and a lack of sediment flowing from the Mississippi River have contributed to the continuing loss.The Deepwater Horizon oil spill accelerated the problem in 2010. Severe oiling along Louisiana’s coast caused a decline in plant cover and marine species production.It also placed additional pressure on the Barataria Landbridge, an important hydrologic barrier separating the fresher marshes of the upper basin from the saltier waters farther south.To restore the damaged wetlands, the Louisiana Trustee Implementation Group developed the Upper Barataria Marsh Creation Project, one of the largest habitat restoration efforts in the Gulf region.Between 2022 and 2023, contractors from Weeks Marine dredged about 8 million cubic yards of sediment from the Mississippi River. The amount of material was enough to fill the Caesars Superdome twice.The sediment was used to create 1,170 acres of emergent wetland habitat. The project also created 89 acres of water features, including a tidal pond and 18,815 linear feet of flow pathways designed to replicate natural tidal creeks.Strategic gaps were also created in the surrounding dikes, allowing water and wildlife to move between the newly created marsh and the larger Barataria Basin.The project ultimately created 1,259 acres of land and water features, exceeding its original target by 76 acres.Scientists are now monitoring the restored area to determine whether it is developing into a healthy and functioning ecosystem.Research teams from The Water Institute have spent long days in the marsh collecting and examining sediment and water samples. Their work includes counting and measuring fish, shrimp and crabs found in the newly created habitat.The research is being conducted in partnership with Nicholls State University, giving students an opportunity to gain first-hand experience in fisheries ecology.Researchers have already detected all the target species, including blue crab, brown shrimp, white shrimp and red drum, using the new water features and channels.Their presence is an encouraging sign that the constructed marsh is connected to the surrounding basin. This connectivity allows tides to carry nutrients into the restored habitat and provides pathways for fish and shrimp to move through the ecosystem.The early results have given researchers reason for optimism.“It’s amazing to already see not just fish in here, but there are tons of fishermen on the water,” said Erin Kiskaddon, a coastal ecologist at The Water Institute. “It’s a big win.”Monitoring carried out in partnership with the U.S. Geological Survey has also shown that native plant species are naturally taking root in the restored marsh.A community effort also led to the planting of 500 cypress saplings in one section of the project. Extreme weather has affected the survival of some of the trees, but the effort is helping restoration experts understand how to create more resilient coastal forests in the future.The importance of the project extends beyond wildlife. Louisiana’s wetlands are closely linked to the state’s fishing industry and wider economy.Healthy marshes are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth. They support a major seafood industry that generates approximately half of commercially harvested seafood in the United States.In Louisiana, the 2024 harvest of blue crab and white shrimp generated more than $120 million.“I don’t think there’s anywhere in the world where you’ll find the health of an ecosystem so intrinsically tied to the health of our economy,” said Jonathan Hird, project principal at Moffatt & Nichol and lead engineer on the project.Although construction of the Upper Barataria Marsh Creation Project has been completed, its recovery is expected to continue for years.Over the next two decades, the newly created marsh will settle and stabilize. As this happens, the amount of time the marsh is flooded by tides is expected to increase, helping improve nutrient cycling and wildlife access.The project is governed by a 20-year monitoring and adaptive management plan. Scientists will continue tracking the condition of the marsh and can recommend corrective measures, such as adjusting water flow or replanting vegetation, if the ecosystem does not develop as expected.The restoration is also intended to protect Louisiana’s long-standing fishing, hunting and birdwatching traditions by providing healthier wetlands for future generations.“When I think about sitting in a duck blind or out on the water and watching the sunrise, I get goosebumps. So many people have the same excitement about this place,” said Connor Gilbert, sportsman outreach and policy specialist at the National Wildlife Federation.
Article Summary: Louisiana’s coastline is showing early signs of recovery after a major wetland restoration project created 1,170 acres of new marsh habitat in the Barataria Basin. One year after construction, species including white and brown shrimp, blue crab and red drum have begun using the newly restored ecosystem.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Zohran Mamdani: 'For generation after generation, we have been told that when the world has sent its people to our shores, it has not sent its best'
Article Text:
Quote of the day by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

My family did not arrive by boat

American exceptionalism

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani delivered a powerful speech on July 4, 2026, on the occasion of America's 250th birthday, addressing the burning issue of migration, weaving in his story of coming to the US as well. "The city I see today looks very different than the one that greeted George Washington. In July of 1776, our city simmered under the yoke of oppression. The British had imposed a colonial rule so repressive that 250 years ago, 80 miles south, a small group of newspaper editors, farmers, and soldiers signed their names on a document declaring truths that feel self-evident now, but were revolutionary then, establishing the ideals our nation still strives to fulfill," he said."The British did not take it well. War broke out. And that August, as the largest battle of the Revolutionary War unfolded in Brooklyn, batteries on Governor’s Island took aim at British ships anchored just offshore. We were outgunned, we were outmanned, and we were soundly defeated. After only a few months, it appeared our fledgling attempt at democracy was on the precipice of collapse.""But that night, with the moon overhead, thousands of our soldiers silently climbed into ferries and flat-bottomed boats and escaped to Manhattan.The Continental Army survived to fight another day. Independence may have been declared in Philadelphia, but it was rescued in New York City.""George Washington was the last to leave Brooklyn. As he waited at the river’s edge, the sun beginning its rise, he would have looked out over New York City’s waters and seen what so many have seen in the 250 years since, an opportunity to begin anew. Those opportunities, like everything in New York City, are not given, they are won."In his speech, he recounted the waves of migration that happened in phases to America. "That legacy of every generation of Americans insisting that the right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness extends to them, too, is no relic of the past.""It carried millions of Black Americans north during the Great Migration. It drew hundreds of thousands of Puerto Ricans to New York City after the Second World War. It invited countless others from the West Indies and South Asia and West Africa and across the world. And it is what brought my family to this city when I was seven years old.""My family did not arrive by boat, although we saw the Statue of Liberty from the window of the plane. Even from the air, we could make out the promise of America, the promise of the beautiful patriotic work of rendering America, year after year, a little more faithful to its founding ideals."Mamdani said American exceptionalism makes freedom more free. "For generation after generation, we have been told that when the world has sent its people to our shores, it has not sent its best. It sent Puritans and Sikhs and Quakers and Muslims and Jewish people who were banished for praying the wrong way, worshipping the wrong gods, angering the wrong people. It sent peasants and serfs from slums and shtetls who were treated as less because they hardly owned clothes, let alone land. It sent immigrants for whom power was something someone else had.""What a privilege each of us has to live in a nation that every one of its inhabitants can shape. What a responsibility each of us possesses to prove ourselves worthy of all those who came before. What power each of us holds to bring America ever closer to the greatness so many have seen when they looked upon these shores, the greatness that for 250 years has been America."
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani delivered a powerful speech on July 4, 2026, on the occasion of America's 250th birthday. He addressed the burning issue of migration, weaving in his story of coming to the US as well. He said American exceptionalism makes freedom more free.

Article Title: Trump announces Karoline Leavitt’s exit as White House press secretary
Article Text:
Trump added that Leavitt would remain involved as one of his “top outside advisors”

US president Donald Trump has announced that White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will leave her role at the end of August to spend more time with her family.In a post on Truth Social, Trump described Leavitt as “one of my most trusted aides” and said he “totally understand[s] and respect[s]” her decision. He added that she would remain involved as one of his “top outside advisors” and an influential voice in the Republican Party ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.“Our wonderful White House Press Secretary, and one of my most trusted aides, Karoline Leavitt, will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family, a decision I totally understand and respect!” Trump wrote.“Karoline has been one of the best White House Press Secretaries in the History of the Office. Thank you, Karoline, for a job well done!”Leavitt, 27, has served as press secretary since January 2025 and became the youngest person to hold the position. In her own statement, she described the role as “the honor and adventure of a lifetime” and thanked Trump for giving her the opportunity to serve in the White House.“Being a mother and welcoming a new baby while working in one of the most demanding jobs in the world has been the most rewarding yet challenging season of my life, to say the least,” she wrote.Leavitt said she had realised that she could not be “the best mom my two young children deserve” while giving the role the “constant time, energy, and attention” it required.“That is why I have ultimately made the bittersweet decision to depart the White House and embark on a new chapter in my life,” she said.Leavitt also confirmed that Trump had asked her to continue working as a top outside adviser. She said she would remain “a vocal advocate for MAGA and the Republican Party”.Leavitt began working in Republican politics after college. She worked for Trump during his first administration as a presidential writer and assistant press secretary before becoming communications director for Republican Representative Elise Stefanik.
Article Summary: US president Donald Trump has announced that White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will leave her role at the end of August to spend more time with her family. Trump described her as “one of my most trusted aides’ and said he “totally understand[s] and respect’ her decision. She has served as press secretary since January 2025 and became the youngest person to hold the position.

Article Title: Quote of the day by David Goggins: 'You are in danger of living a life so comfortable and soft, that you will die without ever realizing your true potential' and why ease is not the answer
Article Text:
Quote of the day by David Goggins.

Comfort kills you

False sense of security

Potential is buried deep beneath fear

David Goggins is a retired United States Navy SEAL, an accomplished ultra-marathon runner, ultra-distance cyclist, triathlete, public speaker, and author. Born into severe adversity, Goggins endured a traumatic childhood marked by physical abuse, poverty, racism, and learning disabilities. As a young adult, he found himself working a dead-end job as a night-shift pest control technician, weighing nearly three hundred pounds, and feeling completely consumed by self-doubt and depression. A turning point occurred when he watched a television documentary about Navy SEAL training. Realizing that his life was slipping away into mediocrity, he made a radical choice to transform himself. He lost over one hundred pounds in less than three months to meet the strict physical standards required to enlist.Goggins went on to serve a distinguished military career, becoming the only member of the United States Armed Forces to successfully complete Navy SEAL training, United States Army Ranger School, and Air Force Tactical Air Controller training. He served in combat operations in Iraq before turning his attention to endurance sports, where he raised millions of dollars for military charities by competing in some of the world's most grueling ultra-marathons, often running over one hundred miles at a time without stopping.He also broke the Guinness World Record for pull-ups by completing four thousand twenty-five pull-ups in seventeen hours. Through his best-selling books, Can't Hurt Me and Never Finished, he became a global figure symbolizing mental toughness, accountability, and the relentless pursuit of self-mastery.Goggins is known for his motivational speech and his book is teeming with such gems. This particular quote of the day encapsulates a philosophy built on fighting against the instinct to choose ease over exertion.The meaning behind Goggins's quote centers on the psychological and physical trap created by modern convenience. The human brain evolved to conserve energy, avoid pain, and seek safety, which were essential traits for survival in an unpredictable wild environment. However, modern society has largely eliminated the daily physical struggle for basic survival. Most people now live in climate-controlled environments, surrounded by instant entertainment, automated services, and endless comfort. While these advancements make life easier, Goggins argues that they also act as a subtle form of sedation. When individuals are never forced to confront extreme discomfort, their capacity to endure hardship slowly shrinks.Living a soft and comfortable life creates a false sense of security. People routinely mistake their current comfort zone for the boundary of their actual capability. They stop trying new challenges, avoid tasks that carry a risk of failure, and shy away from physical or mental strain. As a result, the mind begins to accept self-imposed limits as permanent facts. Goggins points out that the true tragedy of this state is not that a person suffers, but that they quietly waste their inherent capabilities. They go through their entire existence without ever discovering how strong their mind could have become, how resilient their body was, or what incredible milestones they might have achieved if they had simply refused to quit when things became painful.Expanding on this idea requires recognizing that potential is not something sitting passively on the surface, waiting to be casually picked up. Potential is buried deep beneath layers of fear, insecurity, fatigue, and physical pain. It can only be unearthed through deliberate, intentional friction. Much like muscle tissue that refuses to grow stronger unless subjected to heavy resistance, the human spirit remains soft unless it is repeatedly tested by adversity. When Goggins warns that you are in danger of dying without realizing your true potential, he is calling out the quiet tragedy of self-sabotage through comfort. He challenges the reader to audit their daily routine, identify where they are making excuses, and actively seek out difficult challenges that force mental and spiritual growth.Escaping this danger requires a fundamental shift in how a person views discomfort. Instead of treating pain, fatigue, and frustration as signs to stop, one must begin treating them as indicators that real growth is taking place. It means choosing to take the harder path when an easier option sits right next to it. Whether that means pushing past physical exhaustion during a workout, taking on a terrifying career challenge, or holding oneself accountable for daily failures, the process remains the same. True potential is forged in the moments when every instinct tells a person to step back into the warmth of comfort, yet they choose to take another step forward into the cold unknown.
Article Summary: David Goggins is a retired United States Navy SEAL, an accomplished ultra- marathon runner, ultra-distance cyclist, triathlete, public speaker, and author. His quote of the day encapsulates a philosophy built on fighting against the instinct to choose ease over exertion.

Article Title: Why US is questioning Pakistan's Rs 3 trillion defence spending
Article Text:
The US also criticised Islamabad for not publishing its executive budget proposal within a reasonable period (representative image)

US asks Pakistan to improve defence and debt transparency

Pakistan's defence allocation rises to Rs 3 trillion

Defence spending remains a key transparency concern

The US state department has flagged a lack of adequate parliamentary and civilian oversight of Pakistan's military and intelligence spending, while also raising concerns over limited disclosure of government debt and delays in publishing the executive budget proposal.The concerns were highlighted in the 2026 Fiscal Transparency Report, which assessed Pakistan's public financial transparency and identified gaps in the country's budgetary and fiscal disclosure practices.The report noted that Pakistan made its enacted budget and end-of-year financial statements widely available online. However, it said military and intelligence budgets remained outside adequate parliamentary or civilian public scrutiny.“The military and intelligence budgets were not subject to adequate parliamentary or civilian public oversight,” the report said.The US also criticised Islamabad for not publishing its executive budget proposal within a reasonable period.According to the assessment, this limits the time available for lawmakers and civil society to examine government spending before the budget is adopted.The state department called for three key changes to Pakistan's fiscal transparency framework.It urged Islamabad to make its executive budget proposal publicly available within a reasonable period, disclose detailed information about government debt obligations, including liabilities linked to state-owned enterprises, and bring military and intelligence agency budgets under parliamentary or civilian public oversight.The report also raised concerns about Pakistan's disclosure of public debt, saying only limited information was available on debt obligations, including those of major state-owned enterprises.At the same time, the US assessment acknowledged some positive aspects of Pakistan's public financial system.It said the country's supreme audit institution met international standards of independence and noted that its audit reports were published in a timely manner and contained substantive findings.The US assessment comes against the backdrop of a substantial increase in Pakistan's defence allocation for the 2026-27 financial year.In June, Pakistan's federal government proposed allocating Rs 3 trillion for defence services, up 17.65 per cent from the previous year's initial allocation of Rs 2.55 trillion, according to Dawn.The proposed defence services allocation amounts to about 2.08 per cent of Pakistan's projected GDP of Rs 143.6 trillion and nearly 16 per cent of the federal government's total outlay of Rs 18.77 trillion.Spending on civil works related to military infrastructure was projected to rise 7.92 per cent to Rs 363.16 billion, from Rs 336.49 billion previously.Military pensions are accounted for separately from the main defence services budget. The government has allocated Rs 822 billion for retired military personnel under the federal pension outlay, according to Dawn.The allocation for defence administration was set at Rs 10.9 billion, compared with Rs 7.9 billion in the outgoing fiscal year's original budget. That allocation was later revised to Rs 11.75 billion.Major military imports and defence acquisitions are generally funded outside the main defence services allocation and remain undisclosed.The US state department's assessment therefore highlights a distinction between Pakistan's publicly disclosed defence allocation and the wider military spending that may not be fully visible through the country's budgetary documents.The state department's recommendations focus on bringing military and intelligence expenditure into the broader framework of public financial oversight.While the report recognised that Pakistan publishes key budget documents, it identified defence and intelligence spending, debt disclosure and the timing of budget publication as areas requiring greater transparency.The recommendations would require Pakistan to give lawmakers and the public greater visibility into military and intelligence allocations, as well as government liabilities linked to state-owned enterprises.
Article Summary: US asks Pakistan to improve defence and debt transparency. Pakistan's defence allocation rises to Rs 3 trillion for 2026-27 financial year. US state department flagged a lack of adequate parliamentary and civilian oversight of Pakistan's military and intelligence spending. Report also raised concerns over limited disclosure of government debt and delays in publishing executive budget proposal.

Article Title: PML-N set to form 'government' in PoK after two former 'premiers' lose strongholds in third phase
Article Text:
Two former PoK premiers lost their strongholds in the third phase of elections marred by violence and rigging allegations, as the PML-N emerged dominant

Two former so-called prime ministers of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) lost their traditional strongholds in the third phase of elections, according to unofficial results released on Tuesday, while incumbent premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) retained his seat.The latest results came after voting in four constituencies on Monday, with the election process again overshadowed by violence and allegations of rigging. Polling in the remaining seven constituencies was postponed over concerns about the law-and-order situation and is expected to be held on August 21, according to the region's election commission.The PPP won two of the four seats contested in the third phase, while the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party won one each. The latter is backed by both Jamaat-e-Islami and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI).Former prime minister and Muslim Conference president Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan, who was backed by the PML-N, lost the seat in Western Bagh's Dhirkot constituency to Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party candidate Sardar Sajid Iqbal, according to unofficial results. The seat had been held by the Muslim Conference/PML-N since 1985.In Central Bagh, PPP's Zia Qamar retained the seat, defeating PML-N candidate Mushtaq Minhas.Former premier Sardar Tanveer Ilyas, who joined the Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party, secured only a few thousand votes.The result in Eastern Bagh remained pending after authorities ordered a re-poll at 12 polling stations. PML-N candidate Sardar Mir Akbar was leading based on results from 174 of the constituency's 186 polling stations, followed by PPP candidate Sardar Qamaruz Zaman Khan.The election comes against the backdrop of a striking shift in the Pakistani government's treatment of the protest movement that has rocked PoK for months.Just days before the final phase of voting, Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif had described the protesters as "enemies of Pakistan" and ruled out talks with them. But Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's adviser Rana Sanaullah subsequently said 99% of those associated with the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) were "patriotic brothers", promising that a PML-N government would engage with the group and seek to resolve its demands.The reversal in rhetoric came as the PML-N emerged as the dominant force in the election and prepared to form the next government in the region. The party has secured 25 of the 45 directly elected seats so far, while the PPP has won 12 and the Awami Dast-o-Bazu Party one.The first two phases, held on July 27 and August 2, were also marked by violent protests and allegations of widespread rigging, with the PML-N and PPP accusing each other of electoral malpractice. Supporters of the two parties clashed at several polling stations.The JAAC has been protesting across the region since early June, with demands including the abolition of 12 refugee seats that it says can be used to influence the formation of governments in PoK.The group has alleged that more than 40 people were killed during violence surrounding the first phase of voting and that around 400 protesters had been killed since the protests began. The Pakistani government has rejected the higher figure as exaggerated, while Sanaullah has acknowledged that deaths from the unrest were in the "double figures".India does not recognise Pakistan's control over the territory, maintaining that Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts of India and describing Pakistan's presence in areas under its control as "illegal and forcible occupation".
Article Summary: Two former so-called prime ministers of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) lost their traditional strongholds in the third phase of elections. Incumbent premier Faisal Mumtaz Rathore of the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) retained his seat. Polling in the remaining seven constituencies was postponed over concerns about the law-and-order situation.

Article Title: 'Discontent answered with bullets': MEA slams Pakistan over PoK crackdown
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday slammed Pakistan for its ongoing crackdown on protesters in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, calling upon the international community to hold the country accountable for the "gross violation of human rights. "During the bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that public discontent in PoK was answered with bullets and blackouts by authorities in Pakistan."We would like to highlight the human rights violations being committed in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and other parts of the country. We call upon the international community to hold Pakistan accountable for its misdeeds, abuses and gross violations of human rights, including against its own people," Jaiswal said."Over the last several months, we have seen large-scale protests in PoK, including during and before the elections. Public discontent was answered with bullets, blackouts, repression and oppression. More than 90 people have been killed and many more injured. This has made news across the world," he added.Also Read | 'Arunachal is integral part of India, nothing can change this': MEA on China's fresh 'objections' The remarks came as at least 90 people, including protesters, security personnel and bystanders, were killed in clashes during June and July.The banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) has been staging protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) since June over the contentious 12 refugee seats. It has alleged that Pakistan's establishment manipulates these seats to install a prime minister of its choice to lead the so-called PoK government.Meanwhile, the third phase of elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) was held on Monday in four constituencies, amid violence and allegations of rigging. Polling started in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts at 8 am, while elections in seven constituencies have been indefinitely postponed.Clashes between Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) workers were reported in some areas as the region's election commission classified most of the 803 polling stations as "sensitive or highly sensitive".After the first and second phases of polling, which were marred by violent protests and were held on July 27 and August 2, respectively, voting was scheduled for Monday in 11 constituencies of the Poonch Division in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. There are 53 seats in the so-called PoK Legislative Assembly - 45 are directly elected, while eight are reserved for women, technocrats and clerics.The second phase of polling on August 2 was marred by violence and allegations of rigging. One person was killed and several others were injured.Also read | British national killed in PoK clashes; another held for over 2 months, says report The phase also included voting for the 12 refugee seats, which are at the centre of the ongoing controversy.Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) swept the second phase, winning 16 seats, while Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) secured the remaining five. In the first phase on July 27, PML-N won nine of the 13 seats, while PPP won four. With the first two phases combined, PML-N has already secured 24 seats.
Article Summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that public discontent in PoK was answered with bullets and blackouts by authorities in Pakistan. At least 90 people, including protesters, security personnel and bystanders, were killed in clashes during June and July. The banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) has been staging protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) since June.

Article Title: After weeks of violent protests, PoK votes in final election phase amid PTI, JAAC boycott calls
Article Text:
Pakistan’s elections were marked by protests and violence, raising concerns over security, political stability and the credibility of the electoral process.

Polling for Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir's so called assembly elections entered its final phase on Monday amid heightened security and reports of Islamabad-backed crackdown in the region.Voting is being held despite boycott calls from the Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) PoJK unit and the Pakistan-banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).The tussle between the JAAC and the Shehbaz Sharif-Asim Munir duo's crackdown has made the situation grim in PoK.India has also strongly condemned the crackdown on protesters. The MEA has called the so-called assembly elections in the illegally occupied region as a "farce".The MEA also condemned Pakistan's actions that led to the killing of 90 civilians in PoK.Meanwhile, Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) PoJK unit has announced a complete boycott of the ongoing electoral process in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir (PoJK), calling it “unconstitutional” and “unfair”.The election has taken place against the backdrop of weeks of protests led by the JAAC, which has been demanding greater political rights for residents of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.The final phase also came after media curbs, and other major restrictions imposed by Islamabad authority.The demonstrations have also seen clashes with security forces, overshadowing the election campaign.The ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) has already secured a majority in the assembly, seeing a likely return after a decade.
Article Summary: Polling for Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir's so called assembly elections entered its final phase on Monday. Voting is being held despite boycott calls from the Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI) PoJK unit and the Pakistan-banned Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) The election has taken place against the backdrop of weeks of protests.

Article Title: LeT man dies in Pakistan after meal, speculation of poisoning
Article Text:
Qari Saeed Abdul Aziz had played a key role in the planning of many terror strikes, including the 26/11 Mumbai attack

LeT operative was involved in the 26/11 Mumbai attack

A high-ranking Lashkar-e-Taiba operative is learnt to have died under mysterious circumstances, leaving many in Islamabad intrigued.Qari Saeed Abdul Aziz, who was involved in the planning of the 26/11 Mumbai terrorist attacks, collapsed and died near the entrance of a mosque in the Pakistan capital on August 8.Local media reports indicated Abdul Aziz had dined at an unfamiliar location shortly before arriving at the mosque.Within moments of reaching the gate, he suddenly collapsed and was pronounced dead on the spot, with the exact cause of his demise remaining unclear. The local administration has not denied poisoning.Qari Saeed Abdul Aziz, who died mysteriously Sunday, was a pivotal figure within terror outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba, having played a key role in the planning of many terror strikes, including the 26/11 Mumbai attack.Within the organisation, he directed a dedicated division responsible for maintaining active communications and managing financial support for families of terrorists killed during encounters with security forces in J&K. His sudden death has drawn attention from regional intelligence observers. While the timeline between his meal at an unknown location and his subsequent collapse has prompted speculation about potential targeted poisoning, experts note that a severe medical emergency cannot be ruled out.
Article Summary: Qari Saeed Abdul Aziz, who was involved in the planning of the 26/11 Mumbai terrorist attacks, collapsed and died near the entrance of a mosque in the Pakistan capital on August 8. Local media reports indicated he had dined at an unfamiliar location shortly before arriving at the mosque. The exact cause of his demise remains unclear.

Article Title: From 'enemies' to 'patriotic brothers': Pakistan changes stance on PoK protesters ahead of polls
Article Text:
Pakistan PML-N has softened its stance on PoK protesters, calling them "patriotic brothers", as the party prepares to form a government in the region.

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ’s led PML-N appears to be softening its position towards protesters in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), with a senior government adviser now describing the vast majority of demonstrators as “patriotic” and saying the party will soon engage with them.Sharif’s adviser Rana Sanaullah on Saturday said 99 per cent of those associated with the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), the group leading months of protests in the region, were “our patriotic brothers”.“When the PML(N) government will be formed with two-third majority, it will sit with [Joint Awami] Action Committee representatives. Their first task will be to resolve this issue,” Sanaullah said at a rally ahead of the third and final phase of elections in PoK.The remarks mark a notable shift from the government's earlier rhetoric towards the protesters.Just days earlier, Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif had likened the protesters to India and described them as “enemies of Pakistan”, ruling out talks with them. Asif had said there would be “no dialogue with the protesters” and that he considered them in the same category as India.India, however, has rejected Pakistan's stance on the unrest, saying the protests are a direct consequence of Pakistan's economic exploitation, denial of fundamental rights and administrative oppression in PoK.Sanaullah had also previously accused the protesters of seeking to seize Muzaffarabad and Mirpur by force and described their actions as an “India-like attack”. The government had disputed claims of civilian deaths during clashes and accused protesters of opening fire at security personnel.The JAAC, however, has alleged that security forces opened fire on its activists during protests and long marches, with the group claiming that more than 40 people, including women and children, had been killed since elections began and around 400 protesters had been killed since early June.The Pakistan government has rejected the JAAC's figures as “overly exaggerated”, though Sanaullah has acknowledged that the number of people killed in the protests was in the “two digits” and that security personnel had also died.The change in tone comes as the PML-N prepares to take charge of the so-called government in PoK following elections that have been accompanied by violence and allegations of rigging.In the first two phases of voting, the PML-N has won 25 of the 45 directly elected seats, crossing the majority mark in the so-called legislative assembly. The party is in a direct contest with the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), its coalition partner in Pakistan's federal government.The third and final phase of polling for four seats is scheduled for Monday, while elections in seven constituencies have been indefinitely postponed.The JAAC has been leading protests in PoK since June, drawing support from students, traders, transporters, lawyers and social workers. The regional government banned the group in June.The protests have faced a security crackdown, with Amnesty International and the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan raising concerns over reports of violence and calling for investigations.The situation also drew concern from the United Nations, when it called for accountability for actions against people engaged in peaceful protest.The United States has also urged Pakistan to exercise restraint amid the unrest, calling on authorities to respect fundamental freedoms and create conditions for free and fair elections.
Article Summary: Pakistan PML-N appears to be softening its position towards protesters in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) A senior government adviser has now described the vast majority of demonstrators as “patriotic” The remarks mark a notable shift from the government's earlier rhetoric towards the protesters.

Article Title: 'Shouldn't be exclusive club': Pak minister seeks Nato-like Islamic military alliance
Article Text:
"I put the protesters of PojK in the same category as India and consider them as enemies," Khawaja Asif said.

A day after Pakistan signed a defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif on Saturday called for Islamic countries to set aside their differences and form a military alliance along the lines of Nato.In an interview with Geo News, Asif said the agreement signed in Mecca should not remain an "exclusive club" and should be expanded to include other Islamic countries."See, we can't close the doors for other countries. This shouldn't be an exclusive club. This is my personal opinion. It should expand," Asif said."I think Muslim countries should keep their differences, transactional or bilateral disputes aside, on the lines of Nato and stand together," he added.Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the defence pact in Mecca on Friday, marking a significant strategic development in the region. The agreement reportedly commits the three countries to regard an armed attack against any one of them as an attack against all three, drawing comparisons with Nato's Article 5 collective-defence principle.The pact brings together Saudi Arabia's financial strength, Turkey's defence industry and Nato experience, and Pakistan's large military and nuclear capabilities.According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the agreement is "guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states" and their shared strategic interests, defence cooperation and "enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity".The agreement aims to strengthen collective deterrence against aggression and stipulates that an armed attack against any of the three countries would be regarded as an attack against all, according to a joint statement.The pact comes as Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries face missile attacks and disruptions to energy shipments amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran and its regional allies. The conflict escalated after the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran on February 28, triggering a wider regional crisis.A Turkish official said the agreement was purely defensive, was not directed at any particular country and remained open to participation by other regional nations. The official added that it would not replace existing bilateral or multilateral security arrangements.
Article Summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the defence pact in Mecca on Friday. The agreement reportedly commits the three countries to regard an armed attack against any one of them as an attack against all three. The pact brings together Saudi Arabia's financial strength, Turkey's defence industry and Nato experience, and Pakistan's large military and nuclear capabilities.

Article Title: 'There needs to be accountability': UN warns Pakistan over crackdown on peaceful PoK protesters
Article Text:
Pakistan's widening crackdown in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) draws international attention. (Photo: ANI)

The United Nations has warned Pakistan and called for accountability for any action taken against people participating in peaceful protests in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). This came amid continuing unrest and concerns over restrictions on public gatherings and internet access, a spokesperson for UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres said.Asked whether the UN would seek accountability for the reported crackdown on protesters, deputy spokesman for the secretary-general Farhan Haq said authorities must ensure that people are allowed to exercise their right to peaceful protest.“It’s important that all authorities everywhere allow for peaceful protest, and certainly that is the case here. If there have been people harmed for engaging in peaceful protest, there needs to be accountability for that,” Haq told PTI.“The Secretary-General supports the work of his high commissioner, and we certainly hope that the pleas made by Mr Turk will be listened to,” he added.UN high commissioner for human rights Volker Turk had last month expressed concern over the escalating unrest in PoK and called for prompt, thorough and impartial investigations into deaths among both protesters and security personnel.According to the UN, dozens of people, mostly protesters but also members of the law enforcement agencies, had reportedly been killed since June as tensions rose ahead of elections to the legislative assembly.Turk had also called for calm and urged authorities to address the underlying grievances of the local population through meaningful and inclusive political dialogue.The UN human rights chief further criticised Pakistan’s decision to ban the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and arrest some of its leaders.The JAAC, a coalition of traders, transporters, students, lawyers, activists and other groups, has been leading protests over political and economic issues in the region.The UN also raised concerns over restrictions on internet access and public gatherings, warning that such measures could undermine the rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly.“We urge the authorities to ensure full Internet access throughout the territory,” the UN statement said.The comments from the UN come amid heightened tensions in PoK, where protests and violence have also disrupted the regional election process.The JAAC has alleged that more than 40 people were killed during the first phase of polling on July 27 and has claimed that around 400 protesters have been killed since the first week of June. The Pakistan government has rejected the figures as “overly exaggerated”.“The number of people killed in the protests is in two digits. Moreover, security personnel have also lost their lives,” Pakistan Prime Minister’s adviser Rana Sanaullah said in a recent television interview.The unrest has also affected the election process in PoK. Authorities on Friday postponed voting indefinitely in seven of the 11 constituencies scheduled to vote in the third phase on August 10, citing concerns over the law-and-order situation. The first two phases of polling, held on July 27 and August 2, were marred by violent protests and allegations of rigging.
Article Summary: The United Nations has warned Pakistan and called for accountability for any action taken against people participating in peaceful protests. This came amid continuing unrest and concerns over restrictions on public gatherings and internet access. UN high commissioner for human rights Volker Turk had last month expressed concern over the escalating unrest in PoK.
